statement: Lifting static DPE to full adaptive security for policies beyond 1-out-of-N remains open, and the obstruction is worth stating. The Gentry-Waters compiler [GW09, KMW23, FWW23, HWW25] exploits a dichotomy special to broadcast encryption where relative to a recipient set, a secret key either recovers the entire message or is useless. Their two-key transformation can therefore give every user one key of each type and decide later which type shows up in the challenge. A DPE key falls into neither category. Its partial decryption may carry prescribed information that reveals nothing on its own and yet becomes useful once combined with other shares, so replacing such a key by an independently sampled useless one destroys the joint distribution that reconstruction depends on. The two-key argument does not appear to extend to a general monotone policy in a black-box way.
context: The formulation isolates three distinct sources of delayed information, namely the policy, the honest/malicious assignment to its inputs, and the partial-decryption transcript. A future EqDPE construction may handle each by a different mechanism while reusing the EqDPE-to-DPE compiler unchanged. Static DPE from EqDPE. The compiler uses the real EqDPE algorithms verbatim. The fake algorithms appear only in the proof. Fix a challenge message µ. Mode indistinguishability replaces the real setup, key generation, partial-decryption answers, and challenge encryption by their fake-mode counterparts. Selective security for fake setup then flips µ. A second application of mode indistinguishability returns to the real experiment. Because the compiled scheme runs the real algorithms, it inherits the CRS, key, ciphertext, and share sizes of the EqDPE scheme, so compactness survives the compilation intact. The argument follows the strategy of [GY26b, GY26a], with the interface widened to account for maliciously generated public keys and simulated partial decryptions. Lifting static DPE to full adaptive security for policies beyond 1-out-of-N remains open, and the obstruction is worth stating. The Gentry-Waters compiler [GW09, KMW23, FWW23, HWW25] exploits a dichotomy special to broadcast encryption where relative to a recipient set, a secret key either recovers the entire message or is useless. The two-key argument does not appear to extend to a general monotone policy in a black-box way. 2.2 EqDPE for DNF Policies Before diving into the construction we provide an overview of the main tool both of our constructions use. Workhorse: Equivocal Matrix Commitments.
